Recorded in the Amazon rainforest in Ecuador, the conversation explores three advanced longevity treatments Dave and Tim are working with through House of Evolution, their venture focused on expanding access to experimental therapies. They discuss how these technologies work, the early results they're observing, and why some treatments are currently available outside the United States. The discussion turns to follistatin gene therapy, an experimental treatment designed to increase a protein involved in muscle growth and maintenance. Dave and Tim share preliminary results, including a reported average nine-year reduction in biological-age measurements, increased lean muscle mass, and reductions in body fat. They examine why preserving muscle and reducing visceral fat may be critical for longevity, particularly as anabolic resistance and sarcopenia become more common with age. payload.summary: Get Chloe's book The Girl’s Guide To Guts at https://www.thegirlsguidetoguts.com Gut microbiome, stool testing, colon cancer warning signs, ulcerative colitis, chronic constipation, fiber, inflammation, digestive health, and the connection between gut bacteria and biological aging. Host Dave Asprey sits down with Chloe Melas, NBC journalist and author of The Girl's Guide to Guts, to explore what your poop reveals about your health, the gut microbiome, chronic inflammation, colon cancer warning signs, digestive disorders, and the connection between gut bacteria and longevity. After living with ulcerative colitis for 15 years, Chloe shares her experience navigating chronic constipation, abnormal bowel movements, repeated antibiotic treatments, and a healthcare system that often overlooked the role of nutrition, lifestyle, and gut health. Chloe explains why your stool can serve as a daily health report card, revealing potential warning signs that deserve attention. She describes spending more than a decade without normal bowel movements, regularly checking for blood in her stool, and struggling with symptoms that many people mistakenly associate only with diarrhea. payload.title: Jo Chikwe: A Renowned Cardiac Surgeon, on Leadership, Diversity, And Much More
payload.summary: Prof Joanna Chikwe is Chair of the Department of Cardiac Surgery in the Smidt Heart Institute at Cedars-Sinai, one of the top heart centers in the United States, and a Professor at UCLA School of Medicine. She is also Editor-in-Chief of the Annals of Thoracic Surgery, the field’s most prestigious peer review journal. This year she was Chair of the Scientific Sessions of the 99th Annual Meeting of the American Heart Association (AHA). She is a recognized expert on mitral valve repair and a leader of a randomized trial that compares surgical repair with the mitral clip procedure , a catheter-based intervention. She is one of only a handfu l of Black female cardiac surgeons in the United States. This conversation was recorded at the AHA national meeting in Chicago on November 8, 2026, with a live audience that asked many excellent questions. It is the first Ground Truths in front of a live audience, and hopefully more to come. None of my questions were provided to Dr. Chikwe in advance. payload.title: Connecting Our Immune System and Healthspan
payload.summary: In the journal Immunity a paper with an obscure title was published on October 9th, 2026. It was entitled “Single-cell analyses of global cohorts outline determinants of immune aging and link the ratio of GZMK+ to GZMB+ Tem cells to health trajectories ,” which I think is one of the worst titles I have ever seen for, ironically, one of the most important papers in the science of aging. I still don’t understand why authors and journal editors use or allow such arcane titles! In this edition of Ground Truths I’m going to unpack the extraordinary work done by the team led by Maxim Artyomov. It takes our understanding of how our immune system ages—both healthily and unhealthily—to a new level with practical implications for determining its status, and promoting our healthspan. .Schematic summary from the paper This turns out to be a tale of two cells—different subtypes of memory T cells—that contain distinct types of granules resulting in divergent functions. And, importantly, major health outcomes. Schematic Figure made with the help of ChatGPT Share Ground Truths Phase 1: Massive Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Some very impressive stats for who was studied and what was done: —8 international cohorts, 2,609 individuals, 12,394,834 white blood cells —age 18 to 98 years —59 immune cell types from sc-RNA seq harmonization The story starts with the thymus gland, which starts to involute in early life and accelerates after puberty , after which there is progressive loss of naive T cells…

payload.title: The Strange Science of Vibrating Your Body
payload.summary: Whole-Body Vibration, Longevity, Nitric Oxide, Bone Density & Cellular Health Host Dave Asprey sits down with Dr. Tommy Rhee, sports chiropractor, regenerative medicine expert, and former practitioner with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and UCLA Athletics, to explore whole-body vibration, longevity, nitric oxide production, blood circulation, bone density, muscle activation, and the science of mechanical stimulation. Drawing on more than 20 years of clinical experience working with professional and Olympic athletes, Dr. Rhee explains how specific vibration frequencies may influence cellular signaling, cardiovascular function, and physical performance. Dave and Tommy examine why whole-body vibration has become a popular biohacking technology and how just a few minutes of mechanical stimulation may support multiple systems throughout the body. Dr. Rhee explains how standing on a vibration platform creates rapid muscle contractions and mechanical forces that stimulate circulation and may activate endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS), an enzyme involved in producing nitric oxide. They discuss why nitric oxide matters for blood vessel dilation, cardiovascular health, physical performance, and sexual function. Tommy shares the story of a patient in his seventies who reported improved erectile function after several weeks of regular vibration sessions.
